thread:
incident-bot: 🔴 Alert: GPU OOMs detected on fleet (gpu-prod-12 → multiple containers). Root cause unknown, increased 5xxs observed. thread_ts=3254000000

oncall-bot: @marta you're oncall. Escalation level 2. See quick summary in the alert.

marta: seeing 500 errors on /v1/generate -> lots of spikes 50-200ms p50->p99 jump to 2s. Customers reporting failures. Kicking off collection.

eli: I can grab allocator logs and nvml dumps. Do not restart containers yet, want to check KV cache state first.

samir: observed repeated CUDA OOM in the runtime logs even though headroom counters show ~1.2GB free. suspect fragmentation + reserved-block mismatch.

kai: can we route traffic to warm fallback model (quantized) while we triage? That buys time.

marta: good idea. @ops-bot can you flip fallback policy to model=redwood-lite-quantized in us-west-2 for prod-traffic group?

ops-bot: done — routing change applied for traffic_group=prod, fallback=redwood-lite-quantized. New requests should hit fallback in ~30s. :white_check_mark:

grace: customer impact list from monitoring: 12 tenants saw >10% error rate; overall 5xx rose from 0.2%->3.8% in last 6m. Latency p99 increased from 780ms->2100ms.

eli: attaching snippets from node gpu-prod-12 (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T10:01:12Z] runtime: allocate 1.1 GiB request for kvcache
[2026-03-15T10:01:12Z] allocator: reserved_blocks_total=4 reserved_blocks_free=2 headroom_reported=1310720
[2026-03-15T10:01:12Z] cuda: cudaMalloc returned out of memory
[2026-03-15T10:01:12Z] runtime: attempt spill -> triggered, but paging failing: ENOMEM on host mmap
```

eli: nvml top shows memory fragmentation pattern — free segments small (<32MB) scattered.

samir: this looks like the KV cache reserved blocks were pinned by long-running sessions, preventing contiguous allocation for new large tensors. Headroom metric counts total free bytes but not contiguity. Hence 'headroom' misleading.

marta: ok. mitigation plan: 1) reduce prefetch/concurrency on affected nodes, 2) force KV-cache eviction on long sessions, 3) migrate some pods off gpu-prod-12 and drain it.

kai: I can push a temporary config to lower prefetch window and max_concurrent_streams for serving runtime:
```
PATCH /runtime/config
{
  "prefetch_window": 8,
  "max_concurrent_streams": 6
}
```

ops-bot: applied config patch to pool=prod-usw2-serving nodes with grace period 15s.

eli: while that's rolling, I recommend `kubectl drain gpu-prod-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` on the node to force reschedule and defragment. but that will cause scale traffic to other nodes — ensure fallback remains on.

marta: I'm going to coord with SRE. @samir stay ready to run a forced kvcache compaction script if drain doesn't free up contiguous memory.

samir: prepared script: `python tools/kv_cache_compactor.py --node gpu-prod-12 --threshold 64MB` — it will attempt to evict stale prefixes and consolidate blocks.

grace: customer comms: blocking customers A and C impacted worst. Drafting an email noting degraded perf and temporary routing to fallback. ETA for full recovery unknown.

eli: executing `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` snapshot and uploading to incident artifact bucket.

[logs uploaded] link: https://artifacts.redwood.local/incidents/3254000000/nvml-snap-1.txt

marta: SRE is draining node now. Expect pod move within ~40s. Monitoring for further OOMs.

~50s later~

samir: kv_cache_compactor ran on node after drain: reclaimed ~1.4GB fragmented into larger segments. Allocations for pending requests now succeed.

kai: telemetry shows p99 falling back toward baseline. No new CUDA OOMs on that node in last 2m.

oncall-bot: escalation reminder: create incident ticket with severity=high, link to thread and artifacts.

marta: created INC-2026-0424 with notes and artifacts link. Adding postmortem owners: eli, samir, kai.

eli: preliminary root cause hypothesis: allocator tracks reserved blocks and reports headroom as sum of free bytes, but contiguous allocation requirement for large tensors wasn't respected in alerting. Combined with long-lived pinned KV cache entries, fragmentation made actual large allocations fail. Paging attempts then hit host limits causing spills to fail.

samir: mitigation actions to add to backlog: 1) change headroom calc to surface largest contiguous free segment, 2) add periodic compaction for KV cache, 3) alert on fragmentation ratio, 4) prefer-spill policy to allow smarter evictions.

marta: for immediate customer impact: we kept majority of traffic serving (fallback model) so single-request success rate improved after routing change. Draft of customer blurb ready, will send after legal review.

grace: timeframe: node recovered and traffic normalized by +7m. Final status: resolved -> partial service degradation, no data loss. Customers A/C got credit.

eli: will attach heap/kvcache dumps to the postmortem. Please add any logs you pulled to the incident artifacts.

marta: thanks everyone, closing on-call handoff in 10m. If further anomalies show up, reopen thread. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident status set to mitigated. automatic follow-up in 24h for postmortem draft. :spiral_note_pad:
